subject.title: Feature: configurable bootstrap file injection order for prompt cache optimization

question: Should OpenClaw accept `bootstrapDynamicFiles`/`bootstrapFileOrder` as a core config surface, or expose dynamic bootstrap classification through a context-engine or plugin hook contract instead?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix creates a durable prompt-cache and config API that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept narrow core config
options.body: Add dynamic-file classification and optional file ordering with unchanged defaults, schema/docs/tests, and explicit prompt-cache semantics.

options.title: Extend context/plugin contract
options.body: Expose the minimal hook or context-engine capability needed for external code to classify/order bootstrap context without adding more core config.

options.title: Decline new control
options.body: Keep the heartbeat-only dynamic split and document cost and workspace-file mitigation guidance for volatile files.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow core config
recommendation.body: Add dynamic-file classification and optional file ordering with unchanged defaults, schema/docs/tests, and explicit prompt-cache semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc introduced the current prompt-cache dynamic split and adjacent context-injection config, so he is the best code-history owner for the API-direction choice.
